rubric.evidence: WebIDL, error codes, and Chromium 159 implementation boundaries (WebTransportWriter and waitUntilAvailable TODOs, finalized-stream stats accounting) verified directly against W3C WebTransport TR, Blink IDL/C++ on main, WPT tests, BCD, and ChromeStatus 5235261159112704 on 2026-11-24.

Feature 5235261159112704 is listed under 'Enabled by default' in /api/v0/features?milestone=159 with listing name 'WebTransport send groups and send-stream prioritization'; H1 matches listing name and ChromeStatus row declares full 16-digit ID.

reference-contract.json maps 5 source-derived inventory items (createSendGroup, WebTransportSendGroup, WebTransportSendStream, WebTransportSendStreamOptions, WebTransportSendStreamStats) across all 9 required dimensions.

Explains send-group fairness domains vs per-group sendOrder priority, documents the plain WritableStream to WebTransportSendStream constructor-check breaking change, and notes Chromium 159's inherited WritableStreamDefaultWriter vs spec WebTransportWriter.

Two complete semantic <pre><code> examples covering send-group/sendOrder setup, dynamic reprioritization, and cross-browser getStats() guards. No chrome-platform-showcase demo exists yet (HEAD returned 404 on 2026-11-24).

Tabular compatibility from BCD WebTransportSendGroup.json, WebTransportSendStream.json, WebTransport.json, ChromeStatus, and webstatus.dev, including Firefox < 160 NotSupportedError/{} notes and Safari 26.4 datagram-only group stats.
Every visible source label carries a direct <a href> with target='_blank' rel='noopener'; full 16-digit ChromeStatus ID 5235261159112704.

Single <main>, single <h1>, sequential h2/h3, semantic captioned tables with <th scope>, focusable .table-wrap scroll regions with aria-labelledby and 3px :focus-visible outline, On-this-page <nav class='local-nav'>, Baseline banner role='note'.
Shared public/styles.css tokens and responsive layout; logical max-inline-size: 100% on .table-wrap scrollers and overflow-x: auto on code blocks; verified via npm run responsive matrix.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation table scroll accessibility focus
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic landmarks (<main>, <header>, <nav>, <footer>), sequential heading levels, captioned data tables with <th scope>, focusable horizontal scroll wrappers wired with aria-labelledby, and visible :focus-visible outlines.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: single <main>, <nav class='local-nav' aria-label='On this page'>, captioned .doc-table tables wrapped in tabindex='0' role='region' aria-labelledby containers with 3px :focus-visible outline, and role='note' on the Baseline banner.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table mobile overflow typography
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use logical sizing (max-inline-size: 100%), overflow-x: auto on wide tables and code blocks, flex-wrap with gap on pill lists, and never hide overflow with overflow: hidden.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: .table-wrap uses max-inline-size: 100% with horizontal scrolling for wide tables (.compat-table, .scroll-table), relying on shared public/styles.css for .baseline-browsers flex-wrap and pre scrolling without inline overrides.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table mobile overflow typography
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Apply text-wrap: balance to short headings and preserve readable line lengths and wrapping for technical prose and inline code without forcing global pretty-wrapping cost.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied via shared public/styles.css typography rules (no inline overrides on h1, pre, or code); structured short headings and concise reference tables for narrow mobile legibility.
